score_descriptions.total_core_hours: Total CPU core-hours of requested compute (executor_count x cores x elapsed / 3600). Uses per-job profile cores from K8s manifest, not the global executor.cores config value
score_descriptions.compute_efficiency_gb_per_core_hour: GB processed per core-hour of requested compute (higher is better)
score_descriptions.total_data_processed_gb: Sum of input data across all pipeline stages in GB
score_descriptions.pipeline_throughput_gb_per_second: Total data / wall-clock time in GB/s (higher is better)
score_descriptions.total_elapsed_seconds: Wall-clock seconds from pipeline start to final stage completion
score_descriptions.composite_qph: Queries per Hour -- median of in-stream rounds or single benchmark (higher is better)
score_descriptions.composite_qph_rounds: Continuous. In-stream benchmark rounds whose median is composite_qph (rounds with a QpH); 0 means composite_qph is the single post-stream benchmark. Runs with different counts are not like-for-like
score_descriptions.composite_qph_basis: Continuous. Whether composite_qph blends in-stream rounds that executed different query sets (blended), and the rounds per executed query set id (sets); 'not_recorded' for rounds that did not record their executed set
score_descriptions.composite_qph_by_set: Continuous. Median in-stream QpH per executed query set id
score_descriptions.data_freshness_seconds: Primary freshness score. Worst-case gold table staleness during the streaming window in seconds (lower is better)
score_descriptions.sustained_throughput_rps: Rows bronze ingested inside the measurement window per second of the window that data was arriving (arrival_seconds), higher is better. Rows ingested before the window opened are not counted. When intake_limit is trickle_rate this is the configured offered load, not a capacity
score_descriptions.window_seconds: Length of the measurement window: from the moment every stream's driver was running, run_duration seconds
score_descriptions.arrival_seconds: Seconds of the window data was still arriving at bronze: the whole window while corpus was left, else until one bronze trigger after its last write inside the window
score_descriptions.window_arrival_fraction: arrival_seconds / window_seconds. Below 1 the corpus ran out inside the window; the window after that measured an idle pipeline
score_descriptions.pre_window_rows: Rows bronze ingested before the window opened (a stream that started while another waited to submit). Not part of any window score
score_descriptions.ingest_ratio: Bronze rows ingested by the window's end / rows the trickle had released to bronze by then (released_rows: max_files_per_trigger files per bronze trigger since bronze's first write, at the corpus's mean rows per file, capped at the corpus). 1.0 = bronze kept up with what arrived. Falls back to corpus_ingest_ratio when released_rows is unknown
score_descriptions.corpus_ingest_ratio: Bronze rows ingested by the window's end / datagen rows produced: the share of the whole corpus taken. Below 1 on a default run, whose trickle is sized to outlast the window
score_descriptions.released_rows: Rows the trickle had made available to bronze by the window's end (ingest_ratio's denominator); null when the corpus file count or window is unknown
score_descriptions.stage_latency_profile: Average micro-batch processing time per stage {bronze_ms, silver_ms, gold_ms} in ms
score_descriptions.pipeline_saturated: True when ingest_ratio < 0.95: bronze fell behind the rows the trickle released. False when intake_limit is trickle_rate: the configured trickle, not the pipeline, bounded intake
score_descriptions.intake_limit: What bounded intake when ingest_ratio < 0.95: bronze_capacity (bronze busy for most of the window; sustained_throughput_rps is its capacity), trickle_rate (bronze ran a micro-batch on nearly every trigger, each inside the trigger, with corpus left: the configured max_files_per_trigger per trigger bounded intake and the pipeline kept pace), below_bronze_capacity (bronze had idle time without that pattern: a late start or a stall), none (kept up: ingest_ratio >= 0.95). Whether the trickle held intake (BOUNDED BY trickle: ingested / offered rows >= 0.99 and lag within one trigger) is experiment.limits.trickle_bound
score_descriptions.corpus_drain_seconds: When intake_limit is trickle_rate: seconds the trickle needs to ingest the whole corpus at the rate it held (datagen rows / sustained_throughput_rps); a window this long drains it
score_descriptions.bronze_busy_fraction: Share of the window bronze spent inside micro-batches (batches x mean batch time / window)
score_descriptions.time_to_detect_seconds: AML continuous. Median seconds from the newest bronze ingest of an alert's related transactions to the commit of the rule's alerts on the tick that first raised it (lower is better)
score_descriptions.time_to_detect_p95_seconds: AML continuous. 95th percentile of time_to_detect (histogram bin upper edge, 10 s bins)
score_descriptions.time_to_detect_max_seconds: AML continuous. Longest time to detect of any newly raised alert
score_descriptions.time_to_detect_alerts: AML continuous. Newly raised alerts the time to detect is measured over
score_descriptions.time_to_detect_late_alerts: AML continuous. Measured alerts whose related transactions were all in silver before the previous detection pass (re-raised after a rule error, or evidence outside related_txn_ids); included in the percentiles
score_descriptions.time_to_detect_unmeasured_cycles: AML continuous. Gold cycles that logged no time-to-detect line; their alerts are measured on the next cycle, late by one cycle
score_descriptions.corpus_drained: True when every datagen row reached bronze and silver committed all of them before the window ended: freshness covers only gold cycles that saw new data, and arrival_seconds stops at bronze's last write
score_descriptions.total_rows_processed: Rows taken in across all streaming stages inside the measurement window (gold re-reads of silver included)
score_descriptions.total_s3_objects: Total S3 objects across bronze/silver/gold buckets at end of run. Growth rate vs retention capacity is the key signal -- if this grows unbounded, metadata ops degrade
score_descriptions.query_time_event_age_seconds: Diagnostic, not freshness. Median age of the newest event date in gold at benchmark query time (query time minus MAX(interaction_date), day resolution). It tracks where the corpus's event timestamps sit, not how stale gold is; data_freshness_seconds is the freshness score. Replaces query_time_freshness_seconds, which carried this figure under a freshness name
score_descriptions.in_stream_composite_qph: Median QpH from in-stream benchmark rounds
score_descriptions.benchmark_rounds_count: Number of in-stream benchmark rounds executed
score_descriptions.qph_degradation_withheld: Continuous. Why qph_degradation_pct is not recorded though the run has four or more rounds: the rounds ran different query sets, so the two halves time different work
